rationale: Salesforce developers and admins at companies paying $150-300/user/month in Salesforce licenses are a high-budget B2B buyer: their time is billed at $100-200/hour and they routinely pay for tooling (AppExchange apps, integration middleware, developer tools). The pain — undocumented permission walls wasting hours on Platform Events + External Credentials — is specific, recurs across the Salesforce ecosystem, and the buyer has clear budget authority. All four build gates pass (operational_autonomy=7 at floor, buildability_with_ai=7, buyer_clarity=8, willingness_to_pay=7), and the total of 6.5 technically reaches the build threshold. However, responsiveness_signal=1 (no probe data at all) means we have zero evidence of actual purchase intent, and the single-question signal is thin. Prudent call: stage at validate — run 20 targeted outreach messages to Salesforce devs before committing to build. This is the strongest opportunity in this batch.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a Salesforce integration diagnostic assistant: a Claude-powered tool where a Salesforce dev describes their integration problem (e.g. 'Platform Event trigger can't access External Credentials') and gets back a step-by-step permission checklist, the correct config sequence, and the known gotchas — in plain English, not Salesforce documentation maze. The factory builds a clean web form (problem description input), a Claude prompt trained on Salesforce permission patterns and common integration edge cases, and a Stripe link ($9 per diagnostic or $49/month for unlimited team access); no coding by Youval. Sell by posting targeted answers in Salesforce Stack Exchange, the Trailblazer Community, and r/salesforce — link back to the tool with a free first diagnostic; outreach goes out only after Youval approves. Delivery is fully automated: form submission → Claude generates the diagnostic report → emailed within 60 seconds; Stripe handles billing and renewals. The only recurring human task is approving outreach batches and reviewing any support tickets that Claude flags as out-of-scope. Over time, each diagnostic submitted trains a richer prompt library, creating mild data lock-in.
notes: All build gates technically pass at current scores, but responsiveness_signal=1 (no probe data) warrants a validate-first approach. If 20-outreach test yields >8% reply rate, promote directly to build.
